job.title: [Expression of Interest] Research Manager, Interpretability
job.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. Note: we don't have open Research Manager positions on the Interpretability team at this time. However, we're actively growing our team of Research Engineers and Research Scientists . If you're excited about interpretability research and open to an individual contributor role, we encourage you to apply. About the Interpretability team When you see what modern language models are capable of, do you wonder, "How do these things work? How can we trust them?" The Interpretability team’s mission is to reverse engineer how trained models work, and Interpretability research is one of Anthropic’s core research bets on AI safety. We believe that a mechanistic understanding is the most robust way to make advanced systems safe. People mean many different things by "interpretability". We're focused on mechanistic interpretability, which aims to discover how neural network parameters map to meaningful algorithms. Some useful analogies might be to think of us as trying to do "biology" or "neuroscience" of neural networks, or as treating neural networks as binary computer programs we're trying to "reverse engineer". We aim to create a solid scientific foundation for mechanistically understanding neural networks and making them safe (see our vision post ). We have focused on resolving the issue of "superposition" (see Toy Models of Superposition , Superposition, Memorization, and Double Descent , and our May 2023 update ), which causes the computational units of the models, like neurons and attention heads, to be individually uninterpretable, and on finding ways to decompose models into more interpretable components. Our subsequent work which found millions of features in Claude 3.0 Sonnet, one of our production language models, represents progress in this direction. In our most recent work , we developed methods that allow us to build circuits using features and use these circuits to understand the mechanisms associated with a model's computation and study specific examples of multi-hop reasoning, planning, and chain-of-thought faithfulness on Claude Haiku 3.5, one of our production models.” This is a stepping stone towards our overall goal of mechanistically understanding neural networks. A few places to learn more about our work and team are this introduction to Interpretability from our research lead, Chris Olah, Stanford CS25 lecture given by Josh Batson, and TWIML AI podcast with Emmanuel Ameisen. Some of our team's notable publications include and our Circuits’ Methods and Biology papers, Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet , Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning , A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits , In-context Learning and Induction Heads , and Toy Models of Superposition . This work builds on ideas from members' work prior to Anthropic such as the original circuits thread , Multimodal Neurons , Activation Atlases , and Building Blocks . About the role As a manager on the Interpretability team, you'll support a team of expert researchers and engineers who are trying to understand at a deep, mechanistic level, how modern large language models work internally. Few things can accelerate this work more than great managers. Your work as manager will be critical in making sure that our fast-growing team is able to meet its ambitious safety research goals over the coming years. In this role, you will partner closely with an individual contributor research lead to drive the team's success, translating cutting-edge research ideas into tangible goals and overseeing their execution. You will manage team execution, careers and performance, facilitate relationships within and across teams, and drive the hiring pipeline. If you're more interested in making individual direct technical contributions to our research as the primary focus of your role, feel free to apply to our Research Scientist or Research Engineer roles instead. Key responsibilities Partner with a research lead on direction, project planning and execution, hiring, and people development Set and maintain a high bar for execution speed and quality, including identifying improvements to processes that help the team operate effectively Coach and support team members to have more impact and develop in their careers Drive the team's recruiting efforts, including hiring planning, process improvements, and sourcing and closing Help identify and support opportunities for collaboration with other teams across Anthropic Communicate team updates and results to other teams and leadership Maintain a deep understanding of the team's technical work and its implications for AI safety You may be a good fit if you Are an experienced manager (minimum 2-5 years) with a track record of effectively leading highly technical research and/or engineering teams Have a background in machine learning, AI, or a related technical field Actively enjoy people management and are experienced with coaching and mentorship, performance evaluation, career development, and hiring for technical roles Have strong project management skills, including prioritization and cross-functional coordination and collaboration Have managed technical teams through periods of ambiguity and change Are a quick learner, capable of understanding and contributing to discussions on complex technical topics and are motivated to learn about our research Are a strong communicator both in speaking and in writing Believe that advanced AI systems could have a transformative effect on the world, and are passionate about helping make sure that transformation goes well Strong candidates may also have Experience scaling engineering infrastructure Experience working on open-ended, exploratory research agendas aimed at foundational insights Some familiarity with our work and mechanistic interpretability Role-Specific Location Policy This role is expected to be in our SF office for 3 days a week. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. job.description: Datadog’s brand is entering a new chapter, and we’re looking for an Art Director who can help bring it to life at scale. You’ll build the foundational brand systems behind each of our major areas of work, including events, campaigns, product marketing, and digital, so our team, vendors, and partners across the company can move quickly and independently while staying unmistakably Datadog. You’ll take a brief, develop strong concepts, and pitch them with clarity and confidence, then turn the chosen direction into the components, templates, and guidelines that let it scale. This is a highly collaborative role that is equal parts art director and hands-on designer: you’ll set art direction for your area of work, lead a team of brand designers, and do the work alongside them. You’ll partner closely with fellow art directors and creative directors across the brand team to keep the work cohesive. You bring deep expertise in creating brand systems with a strategic, business-problem-solving approach, and you elevate the craft of your team and the partners you work with. AI is already part of how our team designs, and we want an Art Director who has it built into their own process and workflow. You’re tool-curious, hungry to learn, and constantly evolving how you work as the technology changes. You’ll use AI tools to speed up research, ideation, and prototyping, and to take on repetitive production work, so you and your team can spend more time on concept, craft, and storytelling. You’ll also take the brand systems you build and implement them in AI tools that enable teams across the company to produce on-brand work on their own, with confidence and compliance. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. What You’ll Do: Shape and build the system: Build scalable brand systems in Figma that work across print, digital, and environmental formats. These systems include components, variables, templates, asset libraries, documentation, and governance. The goal is for teams and vendors to produce consistent, on-brand work on their own across events, campaigns, product marketing, and digital channels. Lead integrated work: Concept and direct full-funnel, integrated campaigns, guiding the work from brief to final execution. Collaborate across the org: Partner closely with Brand, Creative Operations, Marketing, Events, Product, and Sales, to co-create from initial brief through production, ensuring the work is cohesive, on-brand, and ready to scale across every touchpoint. Push the brand forward: Honor the foundational principles of the Datadog brand while finding fresh, confident ways to evolve its visual identity. AI is a core part of the workflow: Use AI-assisted tools in your process for research, ideation, prototyping, and production, and build them into our systems and processes so the whole team can use them effectively. Lead and develop designers: Mentor and grow a team of brand designers through clear direction, thoughtful critique, and growth opportunities, and stay hands-on to model the standard you expect. Present and persuade: Articulate and defend your creative choices to stakeholders at every level, from fellow creative leaders to cross-functional partners, through strong visual storytelling. Manage external partners: Direct agencies, freelancers, and production vendors when the work calls for it, and build the systems and guidelines that let partners run our work at scale without losing quality. Who You Are: You have 10+ years of experience at an agency or world-class in-house creative team with a standout portfolio showcasing strong integrated work. B2B SaaS or technology experience is a plus. You have 3+ years in an art direction or design leadership role, managing and mentoring designers, including setting direction, giving feedback, and growing talent. You’re equally comfortable directing the work and doing it yourself. You have deep experience designing for live events and experiential work, such as keynotes, environments, signage, and event content, ideally at global scale. job.title: Account Executive, Enterprise
job.description:
At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires.

Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 50,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.

Over the past few years, Linear has experienced incredible organic growth and has become the default tool of choice for many of the world’s best product teams. We are now layering a product-led sales motion on top of our existing self-serve business to further accelerate our ambitions and bring the magic of Linear to even more and larger companies. You’ll play an instrumental role in defining our enterprise sales motion, contribute to the future of our product, and help high-impact companies build better software.

Location & work mode

While Linear is a remote-first company across the US and Europe, this role in APAC is office based 2–3 days per week, as this role will be closely connected to in-person collaboration with our growing sales presence in the region.

What you'll do

 - Become a product expert and help customers use Linear effectively; assist prospects through the trial and evaluation phase

 - Generate a strong pipeline and exceed quarterly targets

 - Stay up to date with our product offering, industry trends, competitive landscape, and market trends to continuously adapt sales strategies and approaches for maximum impact

 - Build relationships with key stakeholders within accounts; understand client needs deeply, align Linear’s solutions to business objectives + shape decision criteria. Effectively communicate and align our value proposition to decision-makers

 - Be the voice of the customer; advocate for customers by surfacing product or adoption blockers to our product team

 - Help build the foundation and define our enterprise sales process

What we're looking for

 - 3+ years selling to the enterprise, and 7+ years in a quota-carrying sales role

 - Experience selling a technical product to both engineering and product leadership; bonus if you have experience selling collaboration or project management software

 - SaaS and startup experience; comfortable working and adapting in a fast-paced and flexible environment

 - Ability to understand complex client needs, craft tailored discovery, and drive sales through consultative approaches.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, and product demonstration skills

 - Highly autonomous with a bias for action. Owner’s mindset to quickly come up to speed on product, market, ICP, and unique differentiators.

What we offer

We're a small, focused team that cares deeply about the quality of our work and the people we do it with. Here's what you can expect:

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Employee-friendly equity terms

 - Daily meal and coffee stipend on every workday

 - Health coverage (based on country requirements)

 - 5 weeks paid vacation, plus local statutory holidays

 - 4 months paid parental leave

 - Paid month off after 4 years & every 2 years thereafter

 - Regular team events and off-sites

job.title: Administrative Business Partner
job.description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Our team of Administrative Business Partners does more than just support our leaders: we're the backbone of the busiest people at Palantir. We build positive relationships with the people we support and anticipate their needs without being asked. Our passion for helping others makes us an invaluable resource at Palantir!

As an Administrative Business Partner, you will be handling a variety of professional responsibilities, including calendaring, travel, and expenses. You are very organized and thrive off of enabling the people we support to be as productive and impactful as possible. You'll demonstrate your excellent communication skills, and exercise tact and diplomacy in helping to manage relationships with internal and external senior team members at Palantir. In this role you'll also demonstrate good judgment and critical thinking by understanding competing priorities and actioning accordingly.
 Life at Palantir
 
We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
 
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
 
If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process, please reach out and let us know how we can help.
 
Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

job.title: American Tech Fellowship
job.description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, power decisions on the battlefield, locate missing children, and more.
 
Applications for the January 2027 cohort are open now through December 11, 2026. 
 
The Program
 
In the 20th century, America pioneered mass production. We built the Arsenal of Democracy and won the war. Then we left this mighty Arsenal to rust. Silicon Valley, a product of Heartland work ethic, turned its back on the American worker.

It's time to reawaken the giant.

The same spirit of practical innovation that enabled America to dominate the previous century lives on in every American factory, workshop, and garage today. Some fear the proliferation of Artificial Intelligence, but we see the opportunity for a technological and industrial renaissance.

Palantir is launching the American Tech Fellowship to arm Americans with the skills to deploy cutting-edge software in the workforce. You will have an opportunity to explore and build on Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) and earn a professional certification in its use. Exceptional performers will earn an opportunity to interview for a role at Palantir or partner companies, where you can use your newfound skills to contribute to the revival of American industry.

This fellowship is about more than careers. It's about restoring the promise that hard work and determination can still change your life in America. It's an investment in American excellence, and evidence of our belief that America's greatest builders are still to be discovered.

The American worker, given the right tools and opportunity, remains our competitive advantage. It's time to prove it.
 
The Role
 
In this fellowship, you'll participate in a comprehensive training program with our partner, Ontologize, to level up your technical skills on Foundry and AIP. You'll learn how to deploy Palantir's advanced software to solve tough problems in enterprise settings and have the opportunity to engage directly with Palantir engineers and leadership.

The fellowship runs for 12 weeks, beginning on January 13, 2027. You are expected to attend live virtual sessions on two weeknights each week. We will also have optional sessions once a week and office hours throughout the duration of the program. Expect to spend 10 to 15 hours per week on instruction and project work throughout the fellowship. 

This program provides valuable training to participants and is unpaid.

The window for submitting American Tech Fellowship applications is now through December 11, 2026.

Our Product Development organisation is made up of small teams of Software Engineers. Each team focuses on a specific aspect of a product and work collaboratively to build cross functional capabilities, streamline user workflows and continuously improve our software's efficiency and reliability.
 
We’re hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering both developers and end-users to work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, and scalable systems, and to design robust APIs and primitives, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our products and the people who use them.
 
Frontline
 
Foundry Software Engineers may be offered the opportunity to Frontline, an exclusive program unlike any other. This unique, short-term assignment involves being embedded with customers, allowing you to work directly with users and gain firsthand insight into how our products are used and the challenges our customers face. Unlike traditional engineering roles, Frontline immerses you in complex, ambiguous problems, empowering you to deliver impactful solutions across some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.
 
Some of our most successful products were built on the factory floor, addressing real-world problems for the world's most important institutions. These products were developed by some of our most successful product engineers, who began their careers in roles aligned with Frontline responsibilities, gaining a deep understanding of both our technology and our customers.
 
Frontliners operate across a broad spectrum of responsibilities, much like a startup CTO. They work in small teams to own the end-to-end execution of high-stakes projects. This spectrum ranges from discussing architecture and building custom web apps to conducting workshops with users and strategizing with customer executives. No two days are alike, as each day is diverse and impactful. By witnessing how customers engage with Foundry and experiencing these pain points firsthand, you’ll gain unique insights that feed directly back into our development process, helping to refine and enhance our products.

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Platform Intelligence Engineers are the engine behind Palantir’s most strategic and important operations. Engineers are responsible for designing, creating, and maintaining the critical data infrastructure layer that powers decision-making across the business. This infrastructure enables teams to understand product usage, stability trends, cost efficiency, value creation, revenue streams, and more.
 
As an Intelligence Engineer, you will partner with teammates and leaders across the business to address, measure, and evaluate Palantir’s internal strategic and tactical performance. You will keep business outcomes in mind as you develop data pipelines, perform analysis, and work with stakeholders to operationalize insights that propel the business forward.
 
Depending on which team you join, you might analyze cloud utilization, user metrics, stability KPIs, cost optimizations, or even model pricing changes all while ensuring best in class support for our partner teams.
 
You will use Palantir’s platforms, just as Palantir’s customers do, to clean and enrich troves of data from disparate sources, allowing you to unlock key insights, create visualizations and custom applications that help drive day-to-day outcomes. Teams across Palantir will consult with and rely on you to help guide planning and decision-making for a wide range of topics while balancing various sets of priorities and weighing costs.
 
About You
 
You are proficient in Python and have experience in a previous or current job writing code on a day-to-day basis. You understand the challenges of finding the right data to answer a problem, cleaning data, and then distilling findings to executive-level insights under extreme time pressure. You are a master data manipulator — able to design systems, implement pipelines, decomp existing codebases, and clearly present findings to leadership.
 
You are a problem solver who loves gathering information from various sources, analyzing and presenting your recommendations to technical teams, business partners, and Palantir leadership. You are a top-level communicator who thrives in both cross-timezone collaborations as well as individual projects. You feel comfortable working in a data-rich and dynamic environment, putting various pieces of the puzzle together to create a coherent picture.
 
This position will offer an exciting work environment, wide-ranging exposure, and a chance to create a measurable impact on Palantir’s operations, customer satisfaction and bottom line.

job.description:
Perplexity is seeking a self-starting, technically fluent Account Executive to join our small but mighty Enterprise team and own new business for the Perplexity API platform — the frontier AI developer tools (Search, Sonar, and Agent APIs) that power real-time, grounded answer engines.

This is a rare seat. You'll get to sell — and help shape — frontier AI dev tools, with a front-row seat into how the most ambitious AI-native product companies think about frontier AI infrastructure. Your job is to evangelize that platform with large enterprises and turn it into durable revenue. This role is ideal for proactive sales professionals who thrive at the intersection of technology and business, can operate in ambiguity, and want to shape the future of enterprise AI.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Drive new business by prospecting, pitching, and closing Perplexity API platform solutions with large organizations

 - Research prospects, develop account strategies, and execute outreach campaigns tailored to company and industry needs

 - Conduct high-impact product demonstrations and respond to RFPs and technical inquiries

 - Lead client engagement through the entire sales cycle — from initial presentation, technical evaluation, negotiation, to closing and onboarding

 - Build and nurture senior-level relationships across enterprise clients, championing Perplexity's value proposition and customer outcomes

 - Partner closely with Product, DevRel, and Engineering to ensure customer success, solution fit, and a feedback loop into the roadmap

 - Maintain up-to-date knowledge of Perplexity's platform, industry trends, and competitor landscape

 - Meet or exceed individual and team revenue targets on a monthly and quarterly basis

 - Maintain accurate records of pipeline and account activity using CRM tools


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - A self-starter who can operate in ambiguity and knock down walls to get deals done

 - Technically fluent — comfortable speaking credibly with developers and technical buyers

 - 3+ years of full-cycle SaaS sales experience, ideally with enterprise-level clients

 - Proven record of meeting or exceeding revenue targets in a high-growth environment

 - Skilled at complex sales cycles, tailoring messaging to different buyer personas and decision makers

 - Proven success outbound prospecting to large enterprise

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication; comfortable presenting to C-suite executives

 - Adept at identifying client pain points and mapping solutions that drive business value

 - Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and technical stakeholders

 - Experience with CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce)

 - Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience working with APIs or developer platforms

 - A computer science or technical background

 - Familiarity with the AI / LLM / agent ecosystem

job.title: AI Strategist, Legal
job.description:
Perplexity is an AI-powered answer engine founded in December 2022 and growing rapidly as one of the world's leading AI platforms. Perplexity has raised over $1B in venture investment from some of the world's most visionary and successful leaders, including Elad Gil, Daniel Gross, Jeff Bezos, Accel, IVP, NEA, NVIDIA, Samsung, and many more. Our objective is to build accurate, trustworthy AI that powers decision-making for people and assistive AI wherever decisions are being made.



Throughout human history, change and innovation have always been driven by curious people. Today, curious people use Perplexity to answer more than 780 million queries every month—a number that's growing rapidly for one simple reason: everyone can be curious.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Perplexity is building the AI platform for professional legal work: Perplexity Computer, our agentic platform that navigates tools, completes multi-step workflows, and connects to the case law, statutes, filings, contracts, and internal documents that legal professionals already rely on, and our API Platform, which powers search, retrieval, and automation across structured and unstructured legal data.



At the center of this is our Applied AI / Forward Deployed motion: we work closely with law firms and in-house legal teams to distill their core legal processes and embed them into bespoke solutions built on our platform. That means sitting with partners, associates, and counsel to understand how they research, review, draft, and advise, then translating those workflows into custom skills, agents, and connector configurations that run inside their daily process—and feeding what we learn back into the product so it compounds across customers.



As an AI Strategist on our Applied AI team focused on the legal vertical, you are the subject matter expert who makes this real for legal professionals. This is a commercial and sales engineering role: you will own strategic customer engagements end to end—leading discovery, defining what to build, demonstrating frontier capabilities against real legal workflows, and driving deployments from first conversation through production and expansion. You are part customer owner, part product strategist, part sales engineer—fluent in both the language of the practice group and the language of the platform.


RESPONSIBILITIES


OWN STRATEGIC LEGAL ENGAGEMENTS

 - Lead discovery with law firms and in-house legal departments: what matters to the practice, what problems they are solving, and which workflows are worth automating

 - Define scope—what is the right thing to build—and own success metrics, pilot design, and commercial structure

 - Drive deployment and rollout across practice groups and legal departments, with real revenue responsibility alongside Sales


BE THE DEMO AND TECHNICAL PROOF ENGINE

 - Build and deliver compelling, workflow-specific demonstrations: legal research, contract review and analysis, due diligence, drafting, deposition and discovery summarization, regulatory monitoring

 - Prototype workflows, skills, and connector configurations hands-on in Perplexity Computer and the API Platform to prove value in the customer's own use cases

 - Run pilots and evaluations that hold up to scrutiny from skeptical partners and general counsel


BRING DOMAIN JUDGMENT TO THE PRODUCT

 - Translate how practice groups, legal departments, and legal ops teams actually work into product, connector, and data-partnership priorities

 - Assess whether we have the right research, contract, docket, and document-management integrations to serve each legal segment—and drive the roadmap where we do not

 - Codify repeatable engagement patterns: discovery templates, practice-specific reference workflows, demo libraries, and deployment playbooks


OPERATE AS THE COMMERCIAL LEAD

 - Own senior relationships with partners, general counsel, and legal-innovation leaders; move engagements through qualification, scoping, proposal, pricing, legal, and close

 - Create urgency, write crisp follow-ups, and know when to push and when to wait


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of direct experience practicing law at a leading firm or in-house—litigation, transactional, or regulatory—or in legal ops / legal innovation with deep workflow exposure; you have run diligence, drafted and negotiated agreements, and lived the workflows you will now automate

 - 5+ years of total experience spanning legal and some combination of technical GTM, sales engineering, solutions architecture, AI product strategy, or applied AI with customer exposure

 - Deep fluency in legal workflows: research, contract review, diligence, drafting, discovery, regulatory analysis, and matter management

 - Strong intuition for AI products, agents, and workflows, with the ability to understand technical systems without needing every detail pre-digested

 - Demonstrated ability to turn ambiguous customer problems into scoped, executable deployment plans with clear success metrics

 - Strong commercial instincts and comfort operating with partners, general counsel, CIOs, and heads of innovation

 - Excellent written and verbal communication; able to write proposals, customer memos, technical scopes, and launch narratives

 - High agency and low ego, with the ability to run multiple complex customer workstreams in parallel and make progress before the playbook exists


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - JD and bar admission

 - Hands-on experience building with agentic systems, tool-use workflows, MCP, or LLM APIs

 - Working knowledge of legal technology platforms: Westlaw, LexisNexis, iManage, NetDocuments, Relativity, Ironclad, or similar

 - Experience selling or deploying technology into law firms or regulated enterprises, including outside-counsel guidelines, privilege, and security review

 - Founder or early-startup operating experience

 - Strong network across AmLaw 100 firms and Fortune 500 legal departments



If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed above.

job.title: Applied AI Architect, Perplexity Computer
job.description:
Perplexity is seeking an Applied AI Architect to help our customers turn Perplexity Computer into working solutions that drive measurable impact. This role is ideal for technical, consultative professionals who have led complex software implementations and can move comfortably between customer discovery, solution design, hands-on delivery, and executive communication.

About the role

Perplexity Computer is a new class of AI system that navigates tools, interacts with applications, and completes multi-step workflows end to end. Our customers are using Computer to transform work that traditional software has not been able to address.

Applied AI Architects work directly with customers across presales, onboarding, adoption, and strategic engagements. You will uncover the real business problem, determine what Computer can credibly support, design and configure the workflow, and lead the engagement to a clear outcome.

This is a hands-on, customer-facing role at the intersection of solutions architecture, technical consulting, and program delivery. You will work closely with Sales and Customer Success while serving as a quality filter for requests that require Product or Engineering.

What you'll do

 - Lead technical discovery. Work with customer business leaders, technical teams, account executives, and customer success managers to understand the users, current workflow, desired outcome, constraints, and decision-makers.

 - Design credible solutions. Map how people, data, tools, approvals, permissions, and decisions interact, then determine how Computer can support the workflow.

 - Support complex opportunities. Partner with account executives on technical deal strategy, demos, proofs of value, architecture and security coordination, and engagement scoping.

 - Drive value-backed consumption. Identify high-value, repeatable workflows; define the expected business outcomes and usage patterns; and partner with Sales and Customer Success to move customers from technical validation to sustained production use and expansion.

 - Build hands-on. Configure, prototype, test, and iterate on Computer skills and workflows, including connectors, permissions, and adjacent tooling.

 - Accelerate onboarding and adoption. Provide second-level technical consultation to customer success managers and deliver bounded technical work when customer needs exceed standard Customer Success coverage.

 - Run strategic engagements. Establish scope, customer commitments, milestones, success criteria, working cadence, and exit criteria, then lead the work through closure.

 - Improve technical escalation. Validate product and engineering needs and produce decision-ready requests with clear evidence, constraints, impact, and acceptance criteria.

 - Turn every engagement into leverage. Convert repeated customer needs into reusable workflows, implementation patterns, demos, guidance, and product feedback.

What we're looking for

The strongest Applied AI Architects combine technical depth, consultative problem solving, and disciplined engagement delivery. You should be comfortable working hands-on with the product, advising customer executives, and managing the details required to deliver a successful outcome.

Must-haves

 - 5+ years in a customer-facing technical role such as solutions architecture, senior sales engineering, AI implementation, forward deployed work, technical consulting, or technical program leadership.

 - Proven consultative discovery skills. You can turn an ambiguous request into a clear business problem, technical approach, and delivery plan.

 - Hands-on technical fluency. You are comfortable with APIs, integrations, authentication, identity, permissions, connectors, data flows, and technical troubleshooting.

 - Experience delivering complex implementations. You have managed scope, stakeholders, milestones, risk, expectations, and closure.

 - Strong solution judgment. You can distinguish education, configuration, implementation, support, product, and engineering problems and recommend the right path.

 - Commercial and consumption awareness. You can connect solution design and technical decisions to time to value, usage, credit consumption, customer economics, and expansion potential.

 - Executive-credible communication. You can explain technical trade-offs to senior decision-makers while working effectively with practitioners and engineers.

 - High agency in ambiguity. You can establish direction without waiting for perfect requirements, challenge weak assumptions, and make thoughtful decisions quickly.

 - AI-native working style. You use frontier models and AI tools regularly and have developed strong intuition for what current systems can and cannot do reliably.

Nice-to-haves

 - Experience deploying agents or multi-step LLM workflows in complex enterprise environments.

 - Experience with Computer, MCP, enterprise identity, security, permissions, or workflow orchestration.

 - Experience in regulated or workflow-intensive industries such as legal, financial services, healthcare, or technology.

 - Prior forward deployed engineering, Applied AI, deployment strategist, solutions architecture, or technical consulting experience at an AI or enterprise software company.

 - A track record of turning customer implementations into reusable technical assets or product improvements.

job.title: Brand Designer, Growth
job.description:
We're looking for a Growth Brand Designer to sit at the intersection of brand craft and growth performance. You'll be the designer who makes Perplexity's highest-volume, highest-leverage marketing surfaces — paid ads, social, lifecycle email, and campaign assets — look unmistakably Perplexity while actually moving the numbers.

This is a shipping role, but it's equally a thinking role. Strategic concepting is a big part of the job: you'll sit with the Growth team as an ideator — generating campaign concepts, testing hypotheses, and shaping the creative strategy behind the work — not just executing briefs handed to you. The ideas you bring to the table matter as much as the assets you ship.

You'll produce a steady stream of ad and campaign creative across formats and channels, then work with Growth to read the results and iterate. You care about conversion and craft in equal measure: you'd never ship an off-brand asset to win a test, and you'd never hide behind polish when the data says a concept isn't working.

You'll report into the Brand/Creative Studio team and work closely with Growth, Product Marketing, Brand, and our motion and web designers.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Drive strategic concepting for growth campaigns — bring original ideas, angles, and creative territories to the table, and shape the brief rather than just receiving it

 - Operate as a true ideation partner to the Growth team: co-develop campaign strategy, propose test hypotheses, and pitch concepts that open up new creative directions

 - Own the design of growth creative end-to-end — paid social and display ads, campaign assets, and lifecycle email — from concept to shipped asset

 - Design for volume and velocity: build variant sets, test hypotheses, and iterate on winners with the Growth team using real performance data

 - Turn product launches and GTM campaigns into ad creative that lands on every channel it runs — static, animated, and everything in between

 - Build and maintain scalable ad and email templates so high-frequency asset production stays fast and on-brand

 - Partner with Brand to keep visual consistency across every growth touchpoint as our brand system evolves

 - Collaborate with our motion designer and web designer so campaigns feel cohesive from the first ad impression to the landing page

 - Bring a strong point of view on what makes performance creative great — and push back when a "best practice" would cheapen the brand


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - A strong portfolio of growth and brand design work — paid ads, social campaigns, lifecycle email, campaign systems — that shows both craft and results

 - Proven strategic concepting ability: you can show campaigns where the idea was yours, not just the execution, and articulate the thinking behind them

 - Excellent visual design skills with a clear sense of brand, typography, layout, and composition

 - Hands-on experience designing performance creative at a consumer or prosumer tech company, including working directly with growth or performance marketing teams

 - Fluency reading creative performance data (CTR, conversion, hook rates) and translating it into design decisions

 - Ability to work fast, manage a high volume of deliverables across channels, and iterate quickly without dropping the quality bar

 - Fluency in Figma and the Adobe Creative Suite

 - An instinct for building repeatable systems — templates, variant frameworks, asset kits — rather than one-off files

 - 5+ years of industry experience


NICE TO HAVE

 - Motion design skills — animated ads, short-form video for social, or After Effects fluency

 - Familiarity with ad platform specs and constraints (Meta, Google, TikTok, X, YouTube) and how they shape creative decisions

 - Experience using AI-assisted design and image-generation workflows to scale creative output

 - Copywriting instincts — you can tighten a headline when there's no writer in the room

job.title: Customer Success Lead
job.description:
As Customer Success Lead at Perplexity, you’ll lead the team responsible for helping enterprises adopt Perplexity Computer and our API products, turning adoption into measurable business value. You’ll own the customer success strategy and operating model, lead CSMs across customer segments, and be accountable for gross and net revenue retention across the post-sale book, with expansion targets shared with Sales.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll stay close to customers and the product while building the team, programs, and cross-functional partnerships that help us scale.

Responsibilities

 - Own gross and net revenue retention for the customer base, including renewal forecasting, risk management, and expansion targets shared with Sales

 - Set the customer success strategy, and coverage model across high-touch Enterprise, scaled SMB and Mid-Market, and technical API customers

 - Hire, coach, and develop CSMs across customer segments, establishing a regular cadence of 1:1s, account and renewal reviews, and a clear bar for performance and product expertise

 - Build the playbooks the team runs on, including Sales-to-CS handoffs, onboarding, customer success plans, health scoring, executive business reviews, and escalations

 - Partner with Applied AI and Enablement to build onboarding, workshops, champion programs, and scaled education that help customers reach first value and sustain adoption

 - Bring customer needs and recurring friction into product planning, and close the loop with customers on decisions and progress

 - Engage executive sponsors at our largest accounts and step in personally on strategic adoption efforts, high-stakes renewals, and escalations while building the team’s ability to own day-to-day execution

You may be a good fit if

 - You have 5+ years leading CS teams, with a track record of hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing CSMs

 - You’ve owned GRR and NRR targets and can show how your team moved them

 - You’ve built or rebuilt a CS function during rapid growth, not only run an established one

 - You’ve run both high-touch and scaled or digital coverage models and know when each one fits

 - You can show how your team helped customers move from initial onboarding to sustained adoption and measurable business outcomes

 - You’re comfortable with usage and consumption data, and ideally have supported usage-based or API products

 - You have strong command of Salesforce, forecasting, and customer health tooling

 - You’re hands-on with AI products and can build enough product fluency to understand customer workflows, diagnose adoption barriers, and earn trust with business and technical stakeholders

 - You communicate clearly with executive buyers, administrators, and technical teams, including during sensitive product changes or escalations

 - You’re comfortable operating without an established playbook, using AI and automation where they improve execution and knowing where human judgment matters

job.title: Director of Events and Experiences
job.description:

You will set the strategy, run production, manage the budget, and build the team. job.title: Growth GTM Engineer, Revenue Operations
job.description:
In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and our marketing programs bring in thousands more leads. To turn that demand into pipeline, every lead has to be enriched, scored, and routed to the right next step within minutes.

We're hiring a Growth GTM Engineer on the Revenue Operations team to own the lead-to-engagement engine: the enrichment platform that completes every marketing and product lead, the routing that sends each lead to nurture or to BDRs and Sales, and the syncs that move data from our warehouse into Salesforce and our GTM tools. You'll also put lead and account scores to work with Data Science, who own the scoring models, and help deliver our BDRs' prospecting tools.

You'll report to the Head of Pipeline Operations, who sets the priorities for this work and owns our marketing automation platform, campaign operations and attribution.

You'll build mostly with AI, so we care more about your instinct for go-to-market systems than your depth in any one programming language. You'll measure everything you build against meetings, pipeline and revenue.

Tech stack: Salesforce | Clay | Reverse ETL (Hightouch or similar) | Routing and scheduling (Default, Chili Piper or similar) | Snowflake | SQL | Python | Computer | LLM APIs




WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT

 - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

 - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

 - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

 - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

 - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the enrichment platform. Design and run waterfall enrichment across third-party providers, AI research agents and first-party data for every marketing and product lead. Handle lead-to-account matching, deduplication, field governance, data freshness and provider cost. Publish enriched data to the warehouse for Data Science and other teams to use.

 - Own lead routing. Design the decision logic that sends each lead, from marketing programs or product usage, to Marketing for nurture or to a BDR, AE or Account Manager for engagement, based on score, segment, territory, account ownership, capacity and existing opportunities. Co-define lifecycle stages, handoff SLAs, recycle rules and speed-to-lead triggers with the Head of Pipeline Operations, and enforce them in Salesforce and our routing tools, with MQLs and PQLs on the same lifecycle and SLAs. Deliver the enrichment, signals, routing and alerts behind our account-based plays.

 - Own the syncs between our warehouse and our GTM tools. Build and maintain the reverse ETL syncs, APIs and webhooks that move data from Snowflake into Salesforce, marketing automation, routing and engagement tools. Build on the models the Data team publishes, and make sure every synced field has one owner and every sync is monitored. Support the rollout of our first marketing automation platform by building its Salesforce sync and warehouse feeds, along with the nurture enrollment rules and campaign tracking the Head of Pipeline Operations designs.

 - Put lead and account scores to work. Data Science owns our scoring models, including product-qualified lead scoring. Partner with them on marketing-qualified lead scoring by bringing in enrichment data, marketing engagement and Sales feedback, and help set the thresholds that trigger action. Make sure scores and their reasons reach Salesforce on time and that Sales understands them.

 - Close the feedback loop. Track the funnel from lead creation to closed-won. Find where leads stall, which sources and signals predict pipeline, and whether our qualification criteria still hold, then feed that back into routing, Marketing programs and Data Science's scoring work. Capture the campaign and touchpoint data behind attribution, which the Head of Pipeline Operations owns.

 - Help deliver the BDR prospecting toolset. It combines vendor solutions and internal applications. The Head of Pipeline Operations owns these systems, and BDR leadership decides the sequences and plays that run on them. Implement the vendor tools and integrate them with Salesforce and our data. Build the workflows and agents around them, such as signal-triggered alerts, prioritized outreach queues and pre-call research briefs. Resolve the system and data issues that slow reps down. Supply our GTM Platform team, which builds our rep-facing applications, with the data, signals and requirements they need. Talk to users, track adoption and retire what doesn't get used.

 - Partner across the business. Work with Marketing, Growth, BDR and Sales leadership, Data Science, Data Engineering, GTM Platform and Sales Systems to turn messy processes into durable systems, and use the scores and product usage signals Data Science and Growth publish to drive routing.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In your first 30 days:

 - Audit enrichment coverage, routing rules, warehouse-to-Salesforce syncs and lead SLAs, and document the gaps that cost us pipeline.

In your first 60 days:

 - Ship an enrichment waterfall with measurable gains in fill rate and accuracy.

 - Ship routing that sends every marketing and product lead to nurture or sales within an agreed SLA, with dashboards for speed to lead and conversion by route.

 - Take ownership of the syncs that write scores and lead fields to Salesforce, with monitoring and one owner per field.

 - Work with Data Science to bring enrichment and marketing engagement data into MQL scoring.

In your first 90 days:

 - Ship at least one prospecting workflow or agent with sustained weekly use by BDRs and AEs.

 - Show a measurable lift in lead-to-meeting and meeting-to-opportunity conversion for both MQLs and PQLs.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years in GTM engineering, RevOps or Marketing Ops engineering, growth engineering, or data engineering in B2B SaaS, including 2+ years building enrichment, routing or integration systems.

 - Commercial instinct. You start from a revenue problem and work back to the data, logic or tool that fixes it.

 - Working SQL. You pull your own data from a warehouse (Snowflake or similar) and build on the models other teams publish.

 - AI-first builder. You've shipped integrations, automations or agents that real users depend on, using AI coding tools, and you can read, review and debug what you ship. Language depth matters less than GTM judgment.

 - Deep working knowledge of the Salesforce data model (leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities, campaigns, ownership), and experience automating and integrating with it.

 - Hands-on experience with enrichment and intent tools (Clay, ZoomInfo, Apollo, 6sense, Common Room or similar), routing and scheduling tools (Default, Chili Piper, LeanData) and reverse ETL (Hightouch, Census).

 - Fluency with funnel mechanics: lifecycle design, routing logic, score thresholds, SLAs, attribution data and conversion metrics.

 - Comfort with REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth, rate limits and error handling.

 - Operator mindset. You work directly with reps and marketers, ship fixes quickly, and don't need a PM to translate requests.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Hybrid PLG and sales-led motions: product-qualified leads, user-to-account mapping and sales-assist routing.

 - LLM-powered research, personalization or qualification agents, including evaluation and monitoring.

 - Working alongside a data science team on lead or account scoring.

 - dbt, or production work in Python or TypeScript.

 - Entity resolution and domain matching at scale.

 - A prior GTM Engineer role at a GTM-tooling or AI-native company.

job.title: Internship - Search Backend Infra Engineer

job.title: Member of Technical Staff (Backend Software Engineer, Search Crawler)

job.title: Member of Technical Staff (Senior QA Web Engineer)
job.description:
About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior QA Web Engineer to join our Web QA team and help maintain the quality of the core web experience used by millions of people every day.

In this role, you’ll test the web products and work closely with engineers to find, report, and help resolve issues early. You’ll also look at how the web experience fits into the wider Perplexity product ecosystem, making sure key flows work consistently across surfaces.

 Qualifications

job.title: Account Executive | Mid-Market
job.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Account Executive | Mid-Market at Ramp, you are a proven hunter & sales closer with track record of quota attainment and overachievement. We believe strongly in our value proposition of aligning incentives with our customers and you will bring it to life through the sales process with C-Level executives and key decision makers. As an early member of the team, you will also have the opportunity to help build the sales engine and define the sales strategy that fuels the growth of the company!




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Drive revenue for Ramp, owning the entire sales cycle through close

 - Develop strategies for closing opportunities within your assigned territory

 - Leverage sales methodologies to uncover customer needs and pain points

 - Articulate Ramp’s value proposition by using the appropriate sales qualification standards

 - Own sales activity and monthly revenue forecasting in Salesforce

 - Collaborate with product, design, and engineering teams to incorporate customer feedback
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL NEED
